newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine gvt to buy 5.88 mln T grain from 97 crop.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gvt to buy 5.88 mln T grain from 97 crop.

text.p: The Ukrainian government plans to boost the amount of domestic grain it buys to 5.88 million tonnes from the 1997 crop versus 5.0 million tonnes from the latest crop, the government press service said on Monday.
"The Agriculture Ministry and the state grain concern Khleb Ukrainy (Bread of Ukraine) are ordered to purchase the grain from farmers," a government decree stated.
The order would include 4.7 million tonnes of wheat for bread, 300,000 tonnes of seed grain, and 880,000 tonnes of non-food quality grain for alcohol production, the service said.
The government plans for the first time since 1991 to buy grain for state distilleries to produce vodka, a profitable revenue source for the state budget.

Ukraine, which purchased 8.5 million tonnes of grain in 1995, has gradually reduced state purchases due to smaller allocations in the state budget. It has traditionally purchased grain to feed the army, hospital patients and prisoners.
The government order also gave 30 million hryvnia to state farmers to purchase spare parts for machinery in preparation for this year's crop.

Agriculture Ministry officials have said the government planned to increase the 1997 grain harvest to 38 million tonnes, after last year's harvest fell to 25.4 million tonnes -- one of the worst harvests on record.
Ukraine's 1995 grain harvest stood at 36.5 million tonnes.
Mykhaylo Zubets, deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, said last month Ukraine wanted to export three million tonnes of mostly winter wheat from last year's crop.
